decision: B5 FINAL DECISION (2026-11-22): the English release scope is frozen. This file is the tracked bootstrap+version metadata for the engines Ruke owns: every pin here mirrors the machine truth in code (python-backend/ruke_ml/models/ocr_runtime.py, ruke_ml/models/registry.py, the prepare-*.ps1 bootstraps), and tests/test_engine_manifest.py fails the build when the two drift. Model revisions are pinned INDEPENDENTLY of library versions. The background update check reports stable-channel findings only; it never installs and never activates, so the working version survives active jobs, offline states and failed updates.

speech_asr.role: The SOLE audio/video transcription engine for the English release (final decision 2026-11-22). Exactly ONE Transformers integration; no per-model adapters, no marketplace, no picker.

measured_stack.basis: measured on this host: g103 CUDA probe + g104 CPU probe, pinned revision, offline snapshot (.data/tmp/g103, .data/tmp/g104)

speech_asr.authority: python-backend/ruke_ml/models/registry.py: the speech.asr row for PARAKEET_ID carries the revision, the runtime claim and the measured admission figures; that row IS the selection.

bootstrap.status: gap: the measured ASR stack is present in the project venv but is not yet a declared uv extra, so a fresh machine's `npm run dev` does not provision it. See python-backend/pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies] and [tool.ruke] capability_extras.
bootstrap.assets: the checkpoint is staged project-locally by ruke_ml.models.assets.prepare() with allow_download=False at load; first use provisions with visible progress and verifies files before activation

update_channels.note: the measured build is the +cu126 PyTorch-index wheel; the stable-channel check compares base versions

ocr_paddle.role: The recommended OCR primary (the default); every unresolved page falls back to Tesseract automatically. Tesseract-only selections probe this engine ZERO times.

runtime.parity: ruke_ml/models/ocr_runtime.py PINNED is the machine truth; the dict above is pinned equal to it by tests/test_engine_manifest.py
runtime.index_law: B5 final decision (2026-11-22): GPU preferred. The preparer fetches the CUDA 12.6 paddle wheel (the PaddleOCR-VL model card's own index); the x64 CPU index is the documented fallback for a host that cannot take the CUDA wheel, and the preparation manifest records which build and which paddle.device probe are really there. Placement at run time stays devices.device_plan's measured-VRAM decision.
runtime.validated_from: the isolated OCR interpreter's *.dist-info metadata checked against the runtime manifest

update_channels.note: the GPU-first paddle pin; the CPU-index wheel paddlepaddle==3.2.1 is the preparer's recorded fallback (ocr_runtime.PADDLE_FALLBACK_DIST), not a co-equal channel
installed from PyPI by scripts/prepare-ocr-runtime.ps1; only the paddlepaddle-gpu wheel comes from the Paddle CUDA index

ocr_tesseract.role: The ONLY other named OCR choice (Settings -> Engines). Under this selection the PaddleOCR pipeline is never probed and never loaded; it is also the automatic per-page fallback under the default.

vendor.note: Declared, OPTIONAL source-checkout slots. The release works without them: nothing downloads here automatically; they exist for engine work that needs upstream source.

update_check.runs: spawned detached by scripts/dev-supervisor.mjs in the background on every `npm run dev`; opt out with RUKE_ENGINE_UPDATES=0
update_check.policy: report-only: findings land in the JSON report with the pinned version beside them; nothing is installed, activated or restarted; an offline run is RECORDED and the working version survives
